topic: Tuition tax credit: claim, transfer, carry forward (federal, tax year 2026)

example.note: example, not a CRA rule; a student with $12,000 of income owes no federal tax before tuition because the basic personal amount (at least $15,000 for 2023+, indexed) covers it; provincial credits differ and are not computed

spoken.credit: one thousand one hundred and twenty

sources.credit: Income Tax Act s.118.5(1)(a): tuition credit = appropriate percentage × eligible tuition paid to a post-secondary institution in Canada (laws-lois.justice.gc.ca, current to 2026-09-21)
sources.min_fees: ITA s.118.5(1.1): no credit for a particular institution unless the fees paid to it in the year exceed $100
sources.rate: ITA s.117(2)(a): 14% lowest federal rate; s.248(1) 'appropriate percentage' = the lowest percentage in 117(2) for the year (2026)
sources.transfer: ITA s.118.81: tuition tax credit transferred = (lesser of the year's 118.5 credit and appropriate percentage × $5,000) − the student's own tax; s.118.9 parent or grandparent; s.118.8 spouse or common-law partner; CRA canada.ca 'Transferring and carrying forward amounts' (line 32300 / Schedule 11)
sources.carry: ITA s.118.61: unused tuition credits carried forward to later years, deductible by the student only; carried-forward amounts are not part of the 118.81 transfer (which uses the year's 118.5 amount)
sources.student_tax_zero: ITA s.118(1)(c), (1.1): basic personal amount, $15,000 for 2023 and later for incomes up to the 29% bracket threshold, indexed; 14% × $12,000 < 14% × BPA
sources.education_textbook: ITA s.118.6(2.1) [Repealed, 2016, c. 7, s. 16]; CRA Income Tax Folio S1-F2-C1: federal education and textbook credits eliminated starting 2017
sources.t2202: CRA canada.ca line 32300 / Schedule 11: the T2202 (Tuition and Enrolment Certificate) from the institution shows eligible tuition
